summary: The platform is now broCAD/M, with its selected monochrome logo confined to the dashboard and a matching b favicon. The workbench opens directly without a welcome popup. A newly generated CAD-to-machined-part illustration and real loading skeletons support empty libraries and toolpath previews, alongside the actual design/import controls.
warning: The old welcome-dismissal preference is no longer read or written. Existing preference data, saved projects, installed posts and revisions remain untouched. Loading, incomplete inventories, storage failures, archive views and filtered results keep their own messages.

checklist.schema: No project, UPID, saved revision, machine-package or post schemas change. No dismissal-state migration or deletion. The broCAD/M display name does not rename internal identifiers or storage namespaces.
checklist.events: No execution events or agent-tool contracts change. First-run import, settings focus handling and editor workflows remain directly usable.
checklist.capabilities: No machine/post capability changes. Shared illustration is content, with no modal, focus trap, fake project or placeholder command.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No execution compilation, controller generation, audit or output changes. Empty previews show the new illustration without modifying geometry or intent.
checklist.installationAndStorage: Browser/folder adapters and project/post/revision files remain unchanged. Empty-library artwork is withheld until inventory is ready, complete and actually empty.
checklist.verification: 5929 tests across 526 files pass with two workers after an initial concurrent browser/unit run hit resource deadlines. The art/skeleton update passes 54 focused dashboard/preview/routing tests and five Chromium journeys, including desktop/phone direct import, empty preview navigation, reduced-motion slow-image loading and failed-image recovery. The preceding popup removal also passed 97 affected Chromium journeys covering project save/reopen, settings focus, package installation and controller export. The subsequent display-name update passes 16 focused guide/package-tool tests and 31 Chromium journeys, including dashboard-only branding through CAD/CAM navigation, guide focus and responsive editor layouts. The selected-logo integration passes seven app-entry tests and 27 Chromium journeys, covering dashboard-only branding, desktop/phone imports, responsive editor layouts and failed-artwork fallback. Source artwork and actual headers were compared together; see design-qa.md. Native TypeScript, full production build, documentation/discovery, icon generation/packed-consumer checks, zero-finding lint and shared UI checks pass. Screenshots reviewed at 1440 and 393 pixels; built-in browser dashboard and editor inspected. Software verification does not establish physical machine verification. Combined integration passes 138 focused tests across 13 files and 12 Chromium journeys. Removing the welcome popup initially dropped the agent import dialog; the actual app composition now retains it, and the large-file journey asserts dialog visibility before selecting its DXF and multi-megabyte UPID. The new assertion was observed failing before the fix and passes afterward.

publicNotes.summary: Meet broCAD/M and start working directly, with an illustrated empty project view.
changes: The platform is named broCAD/M. The selected monochrome logo appears on the dashboard, with a matching b favicon; CAD and CAM workspaces keep their working headers.
The welcome popup is replaced by a new CAD-to-machined-part illustration in empty libraries and toolpath previews.
Project and image loading use skeleton shapes that respect reduced motion. An unavailable image leaves guidance and commands usable.
Design/import controls stay directly available; populated projects and incomplete/error inventories keep their own views.
publicNotes.compatibility: Existing projects, installed packages, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. The old welcome-dismissal preference is simply ignored.
publicNotes.action: Choose Design in CAD, Import DXF or Open machine program in Start work. There is no first-run dismissal step.
